page.title: Journal
page.purpose: Show every money event as it was recorded, prove nothing has been edited, and provide the only sanctioned correction path.

priorities.statement: Each event's amount, date, account and direction, comparable down the column
Where each event came from and how much it can be trusted
That a correction is a new entry, never an edit — visible in the record itself
Filters and search, ranked below the three above

states.description: The journal at rest with events present.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
The query succeeded and there are genuinely no events — distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
At least one event has been reversed. Both the original and its reversing entry are present and linked; neither is hidden, because hiding the original would be an edit by another name.
The operator is recording an event by hand. Presented as an ordinary adapter path, not a fallback or an escape hatch.
The append-only audit trail for one event is open, showing actor, timestamp, prior value and reason for every change.

elements.name: Journal
elements.description: One row per money event, with amount, date, account and direction. The column of amounts is the page's primary comparison surface.
Per-event basis — authoritative, derived, or operator-asserted — shown in the row rather than behind a hover.
The adapter that produced the event and when it was fetched. An operator-entered event names the operator.
On a reversed event, the link to its reversing entry, and on a reversing entry, the link back to what it reverses.
Why the reversal was made. Required at write time, so it can never be absent on a reversed pair.

elements.name: Reverse
elements.description: The only sanctioned correction path. There is deliberately no edit or delete control anywhere on this page.

elements.name: Audit trail
elements.description: Append-only history for one event: actor, timestamp, prior value, and reason for each change.

elements.name: Record an event
elements.description: Operator entry, presented as an ordinary ingestion path with the same fields any adapter supplies.
First-run guidance: no events yet, and the two ways to add them — record one by hand or run an adapter.

claims.statement: The only correction affordance on an event is reversal; no edit or delete control is offered anywhere on this page.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-002. The journal is append-only. Offering an edit control that the API would refuse teaches the wrong model and invites the endpoint to be added later.

claims.statement: A reversed event and its reversing entry are both present and linked to each other; neither is hidden or collapsed away.
claims.rationale: Hiding the original would make reversal indistinguishable from an edit, which defeats the append-only guarantee at the presentation layer.

claims.statement: The append-only audit trail for an event — actor, timestamp, prior value, reason — is reachable from the journal.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-007. An audit trail that exists in the database but has no surface cannot be checked by the person it protects.

claims.statement: Every event row carries its basis and its source alongside the amount.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-005 and the PRD honesty rule. A figure whose trustworthiness is one click away is a figure that will be read as fully trustworthy.

claims.statement: Recording an event by hand uses the same fields and the same prominence as any other ingestion path.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-006. Several real revenue sources have no API at all. Presenting manual entry as a degraded path tells those users they are using the product wrong.

claims.statement: The empty journal explains both ways to add an event rather than rendering a blank table.
claims.rationale: First-run is the most likely empty state and the next action is not guessable from an empty grid.

claims.statement: The reversal control is operable from the keyboard.
claims.rationale: It is the only correction path in the product; a correction that requires a pointer is not always available.

claims.statement: Amounts in the journal share a decimal alignment and use tabular numerals, so magnitudes are comparable down the column.
claims.rationale: DESIGN.md binding adaptation. This is the page where the comparison-across-rows property matters most, and proportional digits defeat it silently.

claims.statement: An outflow is distinguished from an inflow by a sign and a label, not by tint alone.
claims.rationale: PRD accessibility rule. A red tint is invisible to a substantial fraction of readers and meaningless to a screen reader.
